books.section: Topic 6.12 Controversies over the Role of Government in the Gilded Age
The Silver Issue and the Populist Movement

stimulus.text:
People’s (Populist) Party, Omaha Platform, July 4, 1892:

“Third.—We believe that the time has come when the railroad corporations will either own the people or the people must own the railroads, and should the government enter upon the work of owning and managing all railroads, we should favor an amendment to the Constitution by which all persons engaged in the government service shall be placed under a civil-service regulation of the most rigid character, so as to prevent the increase of the power of the national administration by the use of such additional government employes.”

“FINANCE.—We demand a national currency, safe, sound, and flexible, issued by the general government only, a full legal tender for all debts, public and private, and that without the use of banking corporations, a just, equitable, and efficient means of distribution direct to the people, at a tax not to exceed 2 per cent. per annum, to be provided as set forth in the sub-treasury plan of the Farmers’ Alliance, or a better system; also by payments in discharge of its obligations for public improvements.”

“1. We demand free and unlimited coinage of silver and gold at the present legal ratio of 16 to 1. 2. We demand that the amount of circulating medium be speedily increased to not less than $50 per capita. 3. We demand a graduated income tax.”
stimulus.source_note: People's Party, Omaha Platform, July 4, 1892 (American Presidency Project transcript). Quoted text is exact, including the original spelling 'employes.'

stem: Which of the following did the Omaha Platform demand?

options.text: The gold standard alone, with no silver coinage allowed at all
options.misconception: The platform demands free coinage of silver and gold at 16 to 1, not gold alone.

options.text: The abolition of all income taxes in the country
options.misconception: The platform demands a graduated income tax, not the end of income taxes.

options.text: Private ownership of all the railroads for all time
options.misconception: The platform says the people must own the railroads, not private owners.

options.text: Free and unlimited coinage of silver and gold at 16 to 1

rationales.A: The platform demands free coinage of silver and gold, not gold alone.
rationales.B: The platform demands a graduated income tax, not the end of income taxes.
rationales.C: The platform says the people must own the railroads, not private owners.
rationales.D: The platform demands free and unlimited coinage of silver and gold at 16 to 1.
rationales.general:
Take the demand from the list.
1. The platform lists its demands one by one, in numbered sentences.
2. The first numbered demand is free coinage of silver and gold at 16 to 1.
3. The other choices reverse the platform: gold alone, no income tax, private railroads.
4. A platform's own list is the surest source for what it wanted.
Remember: numbered demands are answers, so read the numbers.
